S: The patient reports a sore throat and swollen glands under the jaw for three days.
S: The throat discomfort worsens with swallowing and improved only briefly with warm salt water. No cough; the voice sounds normal to the patient.
O: Vitals: temperature 37.8 C, pulse 88, respirations 16, blood pressure 118/76, oxygen saturation 98 percent on room air. The throat is red with tonsillar swelling; the jaw glands are tender and enlarged; lungs are clear.
A: Throat infection with swollen glands.
P: Rest the voice and maintain fluids. Take the prescribed antibiotic exactly as directed until finished. Return if drooling, trouble breathing, or no improvement within three days.
rationale: Two Subjective headers. Findings consider the union of all occurrences: the first carries the chief complaint, the second the history, so S-01 and S-02 are both present. Duplicate headers alone do not make a note incomplete. Overall complete.
